exam_context: GMAT Focus Edition 2026 — the only GMAT format accepted by business schools worldwide as of 2026; the legacy GMAT (with AWA, Integrated Reasoning and Sentence Correction) is fully discontinued.
data_provenance: Estimated from GMAC's published exam structure plus prep-provider PYQ/frequency trackers (CrackVerbal, e-GMAT, Target Test Prep, TestNinjas, Yocket) aggregated through 2025-2026; last grounded Sep 2026. Sub-topic frequency percentages are prep-industry estimates, NOT official GMAC-published weightages — GMAC does not publish an official per-topic weightage table. Treat these as directional planning figures, not guarantees of any single adaptive delivery.

topic_distribution_pct_estimate.note: Approximate share of Quant content by topic area, synthesised from multiple 2025-2026 prep-tracker sources.

Q.notes: Over half the section concentrates in just two areas (Linear & Quadratic Equations, Number Properties), making them the highest-leverage prep areas.

question_type_split_estimate.note: Approximate split of the 23 questions between the two Verbal question types; exact live-exam split varies by adaptive draw.

component_weightage_pct_estimate.note: Approximate share of the 20-question Data Insights section by question type, synthesised from multiple 2025-2026 prep-tracker sources. Ranges are wide because DI question-type mix varies more than Quant/Verbal by adaptive draw.

DI.notes: Data Sufficiency is the migrated-in former Quant topic and is consistently reported as the single most frequent DI question type.

marking_scheme.source_note: Confirmed via multiple 2025-2026 sources describing the live GMAT Focus Edition delivery engine.
marking_scheme.format: GMAT Focus Edition is a section-level computer-adaptive test (not a fixed-form exam with a published per-question penalty). There is NO explicit 'negative marking' value like JEE's -1 per wrong answer.
marking_scheme.how_scoring_actually_works: Each of the 3 sections is scored 60-90 in 1-point increments based on an adaptive item-response-theory algorithm that weighs both correctness and the difficulty of the questions answered — answering harder questions correctly raises the score ceiling, and answering incorrectly (especially early, and especially by leaving many questions unanswered) can meaningfully lower it. Within a section, candidates get one review screen at the end letting them change up to 3 answers.
marking_scheme.unanswered_penalty_note: Leaving questions unanswered at the end of a section carries a disproportionately large scoring penalty under the adaptive algorithm — worse than guessing. This is the practical equivalent of a 'negative marking' warning for question-bank / mock-test tooling that wants to simulate exam pressure, even though GMAC does not describe it as a per-question negative mark.
marking_scheme.total_score_range: 205-805, composite of the three equally-weighted section scores (Quant + Verbal + Data Insights)
marking_scheme.section_weighting: All three sections (Quant, Verbal, Data Insights) contribute equally to the Total Score
marking_scheme.question_types_used: Single-correct 5-option MCQ (Quant Problem Solving; Verbal Reading Comprehension and Critical Reasoning; DI Data Sufficiency), plus DI's four other interactive formats (Table Analysis true/false grid, Graphics Interpretation dropdown, Two-Part Analysis linked answers, Multi-Source Reasoning tabbed MCQ/true-false).

exam_logistics.total_testing_time: 2 hours 15 minutes, plus one optional 10-minute break (placeable between any two sections)
exam_logistics.section_order_choice: Candidates choose their own section order from 6 possible sequences at the start of the exam
